reading.body:
Electric utilities are the organized interest lobbying on the GRID Act, which would insulate ratepayers from data center power costs.

The bill carries a bipartisan sponsor and cosponsor set: Josh Hawley, Richard Blumenthal, and Roger Marshall. Its tagged issues are energy and data centers, and its short title names the mechanism directly, guaranteeing rate insulation from data centers. That combination is unusual only in how plainly it states the conflict. Data centers draw large new loads, those loads require generation and transmission, and the question of who pays for that infrastructure is normally settled in utility rate cases rather than in federal legislation.

The lobbying record answers who is watching. Fourteen distinct organizations filed on S. 3852, and nearly all of them are electric utilities or their trade groups: Portland General Electric, the Edison Electric Institute, Entergy, PPL, American Electric Power, CMS Energy, Xcel Energy, Puget Sound Energy, Exelon Business Services, Pinnacle West, and Pacific Gas and Electric. The Edison Electric Institute appears twice under separate firm identifiers. This is the supply side of the power constraint, not the demand side. No hyperscaler, data center developer, or chipmaker appears in the filings given here.

What the data does not say is where any of these organizations stand. A filing that names a bill shows the bill was an issue in the lobbying, not the position taken on it, and the counts here range from one filing to three. The record also does not show committee action, amendments, or whether the bill advances. It establishes only that the utilities that would build and bill for data center load have made this bill their business.

summary: S. 3852, GRID Act Guaranteeing Rate Insulation from Data Centers Act. Latest status date 2026-02-11. Issues tagged from the bill's own text: energy and data centers. 24 lobbying filing(s) for 2025 or later name it.
